name: HTML
shortDescription: The structure of every web page. HTML describes headings, paragraphs, links, images, forms and media with semantic elements that browsers, assistive technology and search engines understand.
highlights: Elements, attributes, headings, links and images
Tables, lists, forms and input types
Semantic HTML, media, APIs and SEO basics

name: CSS
shortDescription: The styling language of the web. CSS controls layout, colour, typography, animation and responsive behaviour with selectors, flexbox, grid and custom properties.
highlights: Selectors, the cascade, the box model and units
Flexbox, grid and positioning
Responsive design, transitions, animations and variables

name: Sass
shortDescription: A CSS preprocessor with variables, nesting, mixins and modules. Sass keeps large stylesheets organised and powers frameworks such as Bootstrap.
highlights: Variables, nesting and partials
Mixins, functions and control directives
The module system with @use and @forward

name: Less
shortDescription: A CSS preprocessor that adds variables, mixins, operations and functions with a syntax very close to plain CSS. Less compiles in Node.js or directly in the browser.
highlights: Variables, nesting and operations
Mixins, guards and functions
Compiling Less and migrating from plain CSS

name: Bootstrap
shortDescription: The most widely used CSS framework. Bootstrap 5 gives you a responsive grid, utilities, ready-made components and dark mode without writing CSS from scratch.
highlights: The grid system, containers and breakpoints
Utilities, typography, forms and buttons
Components, customising with Sass and colour modes

name: Tailwind CSS
shortDescription: A utility-first CSS framework. Tailwind composes designs from small classes directly in your markup and removes unused styles at build time.
highlights: Utility classes, spacing, colour and typography
Responsive variants, states and dark mode
Configuration, custom themes and components

name: JavaScript DOM
shortDescription: How JavaScript reads and changes a page. Learn the Document Object Model, selecting elements, handling events and updating content dynamically without a framework.
highlights: The DOM tree, selecting and traversing elements
Changing content, attributes, classes and styles
Events, forms and building interactive widgets

name: Web Components
shortDescription: Reusable, framework-agnostic custom elements built into the browser. Learn Custom Elements, Shadow DOM and templates to package UI once and use it anywhere.
highlights: Defining custom elements and their lifecycle
Shadow DOM, slots and encapsulated styles
Templates, attributes, properties and events

name: Web Accessibility
shortDescription: Building sites that everyone can use, including people who rely on screen readers or keyboards. Covers WCAG, semantic HTML, ARIA, colour contrast and testing tools.
highlights: WCAG principles and how people use assistive technology
Semantic structure, forms, images and ARIA
Keyboard support, focus management and testing

name: Responsive Web Design
shortDescription: Layouts that adapt to phones, tablets and desktops. Learn fluid grids, media queries, container queries, responsive images and mobile-first thinking.
highlights: Viewport, fluid units and mobile-first workflow
Media and container queries
Responsive images, typography and navigation patterns

name: Progressive Web Apps
shortDescription: Web apps that install, work offline and send notifications. Learn service workers, the web app manifest, caching strategies and app-like user experience.
highlights: The web app manifest and installability
Service workers and caching strategies
Offline data, push notifications and auditing

name: Web APIs
shortDescription: The browser's built-in capabilities beyond the DOM: Fetch, Storage, Geolocation, Canvas, Web Workers, Intersection Observer, Clipboard and more.
highlights: Fetch, JSON and working with HTTP APIs
Storage, IndexedDB and the History API
Workers, observers, Canvas and device APIs

name: Web Performance
shortDescription: Making pages fast and keeping them fast. Learn Core Web Vitals, loading strategies, image optimisation, caching and measurement with Lighthouse and DevTools.
highlights: How browsers load and render pages
Core Web Vitals and measuring with Lighthouse
Images, fonts, code splitting and caching strategies
